target_customer: Bitcoin ATM operators and individuals converting cash to bitcoin at kiosks
problem: Buying bitcoin was confusing and required bank access. Bitaccess put bitcoin in a physical ATM and later sold the ATM operating software to operators.
business_model: Hardware kiosk sales and operating software/fees for BTM operators

founders.name: Moe Adham
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page he also founded Sol Strategies Inc.

founders.name: Haseeb Awan
previous_startups: First bitcoin ATM co-founder per YC page

exit.acquirer: Bitcoin Depot (Lux Vending LLC), majority interest

competitors.name: Lamassu
competitors.traction_then: Close to a third of the BTM market by late 2014 per CoinDesk

technical_complexity.rationale: Hardware kiosk integration with exchanges and compliance tooling; standard engineering with some hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Several competing ATM makers existed and hardware was copyable; software tied to operator fleets created some lock-in later.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No large incumbent entered; Bitcoin Depot bought a majority of Bitaccess in November 2022 and converted its 7,000 ATMs to Bitaccess software by February 2023.

market_need_then: Bitcoin ATMs grew quickly in 2014, with coverage of year-end growth; Adham said they wanted to make digital currency tangible.

identity.voice_and_tone: Simple bitcoin messaging: we make bitcoin simple (YC tagline)

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by CoinDesk, TechCrunch and Ottawa press at the time; no community or merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: A descriptive compound name known in the bitcoin ATM trade press, with no evidence of brand-driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Bitaccess installed its first Toronto bitcoin ATM on New Year's Day 2014, joined YC that summer, and held about 14% of the ATM market by late 2014 against Lamassu and Robocoin. It later shifted toward operating software for operators in over 15 countries, and Bitcoin Depot acquired a majority interest in November 2022. Funding is unclear, but the exit appears to be a strategic software acquisition.
notes: The company website returned 404. Funding figures conflict and are unverified: CoinDesk reported the YC deal as $120,000 for 7% (the standard deal, not a round), an earlier report of a $10M BiT Capital commitment may not have materialized, and totals range from $1.2M to $11.1M across Ivey, CB Insights and Craft. Competitor details rely on search result summaries of the 2014 TechCrunch and CoinDesk coverage; the 14% market share is a CoinDesk end-of-2014 figure. Acquisition was majority interest, not full. Update: no round recorded. Searches show totals from 1.12M (Seedtable) and 1.2M (Craft) to 10.02M over 4 rounds (CB Insights), with CB Insights listing a Nov 2022 corporate majority round by Bitcoin Depot; no round-level source page was opened, so the gap is noted only.
